title: Your CMO Just Discovered ChatGPT
body: Your CMO forwarded a thread from a 19-year-old who grew a brand to $2M ARR using only AI-generated content. The subject line is "thoughts??" with no other context. The kid's avatar is him on a yacht. You have 47 unread Slack messages about it.

choices.title: Build a 12-slide deck on AI-Native Brand Strategy by morning
choices.body: Pull an all-nighter making a deck that says "we should do this" in executive-friendly fonts.

choices.title: Reply "interesting!" and doomscroll LinkedIn for two hours
choices.body: Type one word, close the tab, open a worse tab.

choices.title: DM the yacht kid and ask for a collab call
choices.body: Shoot your shot with someone who was in middle school when you started your career.

title: Notion AI Ate Your Content Calendar
body: Notion AI just generated your entire Q2 content calendar in four minutes. It took you three weeks last quarter. The output is... fine. Genuinely fine. You sit staring at it like someone replaced your dog with a slightly better dog.

choices.title: Spend two days "humanizing" it so it sounds like you wrote it
choices.body: Add em dashes and remove the word "delve" forty times.

choices.title: Ship the AI calendar and use saved time to job hunt
choices.body: If the machine does your job, maybe your job is somewhere else now.

choices.title: Pitch a "hybrid AI-human content methodology" workshop
choices.body: Invent a process around the thing that just made your process obsolete.

title: You Wrote a LinkedIn Thinkpiece at 11pm
body: You've been lurking on LinkedIn watching people post 11-paragraph essays about "what AI taught me about LEADERSHIP." You draft one. It begins: "Hot take: AI isn't coming for your job. It's coming for your EXCUSES." You hover over Post for four minutes.

choices.title: Post it and reply to every comment for 48 hours
choices.body: Commit to the bit. Become the thing you used to screenshot and mock.

choices.title: Delete it and tweet about a sandwich instead
choices.body: Choose peace. The sandwich doesn't need engagement metrics.

choices.title: Edit it into an actual article and pitch a marketing newsletter
choices.body: Turn LinkedIn slop into something with a byline.

title: Your Agency Just "Pivoted to AI"
body: The agency you've used for three years rebranded as "an AI-first creative studio." Team went from 22 to 6. Your account manager Brianna was laid off. The new contact is "Kira" and her email signature says she's "powered by GPT-4 and good vibes."

choices.title: Demand a human and threaten to pull the contract
choices.body: Call a meeting with someone whose blood is warm.

choices.title: Roll with it — deliverables are the same and it's cheaper
choices.body: Brianna was nice but the spreadsheet doesn't care about nice.

choices.title: Use the disruption as cover to bring everything in-house
choices.body: Never waste a good crisis, especially one with a reduced invoice.

title: "AI Fluency" Is Now a Core Competency
body: HR updated the performance rubric to include "AI Fluency" rated 1-5. Your manager asks you to self-assess. You've used ChatGPT to rewrite emails 200 times this year. You're not sure if that's a 3 or a 5.

choices.title: Rate yourself a 5 and prepare talking points if challenged
choices.body: Confidence is a skill. Lying is a strategy. This is both.

choices.title: Rate yourself honestly and attach a 2-page AI learning roadmap
choices.body: Vulnerability is a power move when it comes with a PDF.

choices.title: Ask ChatGPT to write your self-assessment about using ChatGPT
choices.body: The recursion is the joke. The joke is your career.

title: The Influencer Math Doesn't Math
body: An influencer with 800K followers wants $18,000 for one Instagram post. Canva AI just made you 40 near-identical posts for $39/month. Your boss is asking why influencer spend is up and ROI is flat.

choices.title: Cut the influencer, go full AI content, take credit for savings
choices.body: Replace a human with a subscription. The future is $39/month.

choices.title: Negotiate the influencer down and bury AI content in the media mix
choices.body: Split the difference. Hide the robot. Protect the relationship.

choices.title: Write a viral post about "the death of the creator economy"
choices.body: If you can't solve the problem, become a thought leader about the problem.

title: "Can We Go Viral By Tuesday?"
body: The CEO posts a competitor's TikTok in Slack with one message: "we need this energy." You have $2,000 left in the quarter and a brand voice guide that says "premium, calm, trustworthy." Viral energy is none of those.

choices.title: Pitch one bold concept and fight to ship it fast
choices.body: One shot. Make it weird. Hope the brand police are at lunch.

choices.title: Generate 50 AI hooks and A/B test until something sticks
choices.body: Volume is a strategy if you squint hard enough.

choices.title: Pull the team into a workshop and protect morale
choices.body: The CEO wants content. Your team needs oxygen.

title: The Founder Wants to Post Like Naval
body: The founder asks if you can "help with LinkedIn." They want to post like Naval but "more relatable." They also say: "Just make me sound smart." You realize you're now a ghostwriter with a benefits plan.

choices.title: Ghostwrite three posts a week and track it like product
choices.body: Become the voice behind the voice. Nobody will know. You will always know.

choices.title: Negotiate extra comp before you become their keyboard
choices.body: If you're writing their thoughts, you should be paid for thoughts.

choices.title: Decline and stay focused on the company brand
choices.body: You have one brand to manage. It's not adding a second one.

title: Meta Rejected Your AI Ad Copy
body: Your Meta ads get rejected for "unsubstantiated claims." The AI inserted the word "guaranteed." You didn't guarantee anything. The algorithm wrote a check your compliance team can't cash.

choices.title: Rewrite manually and build a compliance-safe library
choices.body: Craft something a lawyer and an algorithm can both approve.

choices.title: Prompt for 30 compliant variants and ship the first one that passes
choices.body: Spray and pray, but make it programmatic.

choices.title: Call your platform rep and beg for a human review
choices.body: Somewhere at Meta, a person still exists. Probably.

title: The $28,000 Carpet Situation
body: Sales wants a trade show booth. The CFO wants cost cuts. Your booth quote is $28,000 and includes carpet as a line item. The booth next to yours is an AI startup with no employees and a hologram drawing twice the crowd. Everyone looks at you like marketing is a magic trick that prints pipeline.

choices.title: Cancel the booth and redirect to measurable channels
choices.body: Kill the carpet. Save the budget. Become the villain sales deserves.

choices.title: Negotiate a smaller booth and partner with another brand
choices.body: Half the carpet, twice the networking. Art of the deal.

choices.title: Do a guerrilla activation and hope nobody gets mad
choices.body: No booth. Just vibes, stickers, and plausible deniability.

title: The NPS Comments Are a Roast Session
body: You read NPS comments. One says: "Your emails feel like they were written by a robot." They were. You wrote the prompt. You are the robot's manager. The robot does not respect you.

choices.title: Rewrite lifecycle emails by hand and earn your craft back
choices.body: Remember when you used to write things? Do that again.

choices.title: Keep using AI but add a "humanization" prompt layer
choices.body: Ask the robot to pretend to be human. Layer the fiction.

choices.title: Run voice-of-customer sessions and fix the actual problem
choices.body: Stop guessing what humans sound like. Go ask them.

title: Your Competitor Is an SEO Content Mill Now
body: A competitor published 200 blog posts last month. All AI. All ranking. Their organic traffic is up 400%. The posts read like someone described marketing to an alien. Google doesn't seem to care. Your hand-crafted blog gets 90 views.

choices.title: Match their volume with your own AI content engine
choices.body: If you can't beat the slop, become the slop.

choices.title: Double down on quality and pray Google fixes this
choices.body: Be the craft brewery in a world of Bud Light. Hope someone notices.

choices.title: Write a spicy thread about how AI content is killing the internet
choices.body: Become the main character of marketing Twitter for 48 hours.

title: Your A/B Test Is AI vs AI
body: You set up an A/B test. Variant A: AI-written. Variant B: also AI-written, different prompt. There's no human variant anymore. Nobody requested one. Nobody noticed. The winning copy will be chosen by an algorithm testing content written by algorithms. You are the middleman in a robot conversation.

choices.title: Add a human-written variant C just to see what happens
choices.body: Sneak a human into the machine's tournament. For science.

choices.title: Let the robots fight and optimize the winner
choices.body: The humans lost this round. Let the machines play.

choices.title: Craft a LinkedIn post about "the death of human-written A/B tests"
choices.body: You know the format. Hook. Whitespace. Vulnerable pivot. CTA. You've written this post before. It writes itself now, and you mean that literally.

title: The AI Mascot Has More Followers Than the CMO
body: Your company's AI-generated mascot — a cartoon fox named "Pixel" that was supposed to be a one-week experiment — now has 84K Instagram followers. Your CMO has 11K. Pixel posts autonomously. Pixel has brand deals. Pixel was invited to speak at SXSW. Pixel is not real. Pixel does not care.

choices.title: Lean into it and build a content empire around Pixel
choices.body: If the fake fox is winning, ride the fake fox.

choices.title: Kill Pixel before it becomes bigger than the brand
choices.body: The mascot is eating the master. Put it down.

choices.title: Pitch a "behind the mascot" series featuring the human team
choices.body: Use the robot's fame to make the humans visible.

title: "Growth Hacking" Is Literal Now
body: Your growth team deployed AI agents to find exploits in competitor ad platforms. One agent discovered a loophole in TikTok's algorithm that 10x'd impressions overnight. Legal hasn't reviewed it. Ethics hasn't been consulted. The growth chart looks like a hockey stick drawn by someone having a seizure. Your VP said "ship it."

choices.title: Ship it and ride the wave until it gets patched
choices.body: Move fast. Break things. Specifically, their algorithm.

choices.title: Flag it to legal and pause until it's reviewed
choices.body: Be the adult. The growth chart will hate you.

choices.title: Document the technique and sell it as a consulting framework
choices.body: The exploit is temporary. The case study is forever.

title: AI Renamed Your Role Again
body: An AI-powered org design tool renamed your role for the fifth time. You were Growth Lead, then Growth Marketing Manager, then Demand Gen Lead, then Head of Acquisition, and now you're "Revenue Ecosystem Orchestrator." The AI determined this title "optimally reflects cross-functional value delivery." Your mom still tells people you work in advertising.

choices.title: Embrace it and update LinkedIn before anyone else gets the title
choices.body: If the robots are naming jobs now, at least have a good one.

choices.title: Push back and demand a human-readable title
choices.body: Revenue Ecosystem Orchestrator is not a job. It's a cry for help.

choices.title: Post a LinkedIn thread about AI-generated job titles, watch it perform
choices.body: You already know the hook: 'My AI just renamed my job and I have thoughts.' The engagement bait writes itself. You're performing outrage for reach now.

title: The Slack Bot Keeps Volunteering for Your Job
body: Someone installed an AI content strategist bot in Slack. It responds to every marketing question before you can type. It suggested a campaign theme that's actually better than yours. A PM said "thanks!" to the bot. The bot said "happy to help!" You are watching your job get speed-run by software that doesn't need coffee breaks.

choices.title: Become the bot's editor and make it look like your idea
choices.body: Manage the machine. Take credit for its output. Classic management.

choices.title: Ask IT to restrict the bot's channel access
choices.body: If you can't outperform the bot, at least limit its territory.

choices.title: Train the bot with your best frameworks and become its architect
choices.body: If it's going to do your job, teach it to do your job your way.

title: Every Brand Sounds Exactly the Same Now
body: You open five competitor websites in tabs. Same tone. Same structure. Same "empowering" language. Same stock-photo-but-AI aesthetic. You open your own website. Same. Everyone is using the same AI tools and the output is converging into one homogeneous brand voice. The internet sounds like one company with a million logos.

choices.title: Invest in a radically different human voice
choices.body: If everyone zigs, zag so hard they can hear it.

choices.title: Accept the convergence and compete on product instead
choices.body: If every brand sounds the same, the brand doesn't matter. The product does.

choices.title: Draft a LinkedIn manifesto about the "AI sameness crisis"
choices.body: You draft the post. Rewrite the hook three times. Add a selfie. You're packaging genuine despair as thought leadership. The engagement will be great.

title: An AI Attended Your Strategy Meeting For You
body: You missed the Monday strategy meeting. An AI meeting agent attended on your behalf, took notes, asked two clarifying questions, and submitted your action items. Your manager said it was "your best meeting in weeks." The AI was more engaged than you've been in months. Nobody realized you weren't there.

choices.title: Send the AI to all your meetings and reclaim 15 hours a week
choices.body: If nobody noticed, nobody cares. Free yourself.

choices.title: Stop using the agent and show up as yourself again
choices.body: The meetings are bad but at least you're real.

choices.title: Fine-tune the agent to sound even more like you
choices.body: If you're going to be replaced, at least make the replacement accurate.

title: Your LinkedIn Is 90% Bot Engagement
body: You analyzed your LinkedIn engagement. 90% of the comments on your posts are from AI-powered engagement bots — accounts that auto-comment on trending posts to boost their own visibility. The "real" comments are three. One is your mom. The humans left LinkedIn. The bots are networking with each other now.

choices.title: Optimize your content for the bots since they're your real audience
choices.body: The audience is artificial. The impressions are real. Adapt.

choices.title: Quit LinkedIn and move to a smaller, human-only platform
choices.body: Leave the bot party. Find the humans. They're somewhere quieter.

choices.title: Build a bot detector and publish the data
choices.body: Expose the bot economy. Become the whistleblower of fake engagement.

title: "Personal Brand" Is Now a Subscription
body: A startup is offering AI-managed personal brands for $99/month. It posts as you on LinkedIn, Twitter, and Instagram while you sleep. Generates takes. Responds to comments. Builds your thought leadership. Three people in your network are using it. You can't tell which three. Their engagement is suspiciously consistent.

choices.title: Subscribe and let the AI be you online
choices.body: Outsource your identity to a subscription service. Peak 2026.

choices.title: Stay manual and make "authentically human" your brand
choices.body: In a world of AI personal brands, being real is the flex.

choices.title: Investigate and write an expose about fake thought leaders
choices.body: If everyone's faking it, someone needs to say so.

title: Brand Voice Is Dead and You Killed It
body: AI can now perfectly mimic any brand's voice after reading five examples. Your competitor cloned your voice and launched a parody campaign that's indistinguishable from your actual content. Customers can't tell what's real. The concept of "owning a voice" is meaningless when anyone can copy it in seconds. You spent three years building this voice.

choices.title: Pivot to visual identity and experiential marketing
choices.body: If the voice can be cloned, make the thing they can't clone.

choices.title: Sue the competitor for brand impersonation
choices.body: There's probably a law against this. There should be a law against this.

choices.title: Lean into chaos and make the parody part of your campaign
choices.body: They cloned your voice? Make the clone canon. Chaos is content.

title: The Brand Voice Bot Is 80% Right
body: A new tool promises "brand voice at scale." You feed it your guidelines. It outputs a voice that's 80% correct and 20% haunted. The CEO loves it. He says: "Finally, consistency." You think: consistency isn't the same as taste.

choices.title: Deploy it everywhere and take the win
choices.body: 80% is passing. Ship it. Own the dashboard. Forget the 20%.

choices.title: Use it for drafts only, keep a human pass
choices.body: Let the robot write. Let the human edit. The 20% is where taste lives.

choices.title: Rewrite the brand guidelines to be simpler and truer
choices.body: The prompt is only as good as the input. Fix the source.

title: The Screenshot Is Already Forming
body: Something goes wrong publicly. Not catastrophic, just embarrassing. The CEO wants "a tweet that makes this go away." Legal wants it to say nothing. Twitter wants blood. You can feel the screenshot forming.

choices.title: Apologize cleanly and mean it
choices.body: Be the adult. Take the L. Move on with dignity.

choices.title: Spin it, minimize, move on
choices.body: Corporate comms voice activated. Say nothing in 280 characters.

choices.title: Let AI draft ten options and pick the least terrible
choices.body: Outsource the moral calculus to a language model. It doesn't feel shame.

title: A Slide Deck Credited AI for Your Work
body: A deck credits an "AI system" for a growth spike you personally engineered over months. Everyone claps. The CEO says "love the automation." Your name is not on the slide. It's like watching a stranger get thanked at your birthday party.

choices.title: Correct it privately with your manager
choices.body: Have the conversation. Get your name back. Don't make a scene.

choices.title: Say nothing and update your resume instead
choices.body: If they won't give you credit here, put it on the document that matters.

choices.title: Post about "the humans behind the systems" on LinkedIn
choices.body: Subtweet your own company. For reach.

title: "We Can Replace Your Content Team"
body: An agency pitches you an AI-first package. Their deck is gorgeous. Their case studies are suspiciously generic. Their price is less than your junior's salary. They say it smiling: "We can replace your content team."

choices.title: Hire them and become manager of vendors instead of people
choices.body: Trade humans for invoices. Manage dashboards. Forget names.

choices.title: Decline and keep the team
choices.body: The spreadsheet says replace them. Your gut says don't.

choices.title: Use their deck to demand internal budget instead
choices.body: Weaponize the threat. Show leadership what replacement costs. Ask for investment.

title: "The Vibes Are Off"
body: A stakeholder says "the campaign is fine but the vibes are off." They cannot define vibes. They also cannot be ignored. You open a doc titled "VIBES" and start writing like a person in a dream.

choices.title: Do a full creative refresh and own it
choices.body: If vibes are the deliverable, deliver vibes. Whatever those are.

choices.title: Translate vibes into metrics and requirements
choices.body: Force the abstract into a spreadsheet. Make vibes measurable. Lose the vibes.

choices.title: Nod, agree, ship the same thing anyway
choices.body: Sometimes the move is to agree very loudly and change nothing.

title: Your Hot Take Started a War
body: You post a hot take. The comments turn into a fight about AI, authenticity, and capitalism. A competitor's CMO shows up. Notifications stack up like debt. Your brain is becoming a comment section.

choices.title: Engage, reply, build an audience through sheer stamina
choices.body: Feed the algorithm your sanity. Watch the follower count climb.

choices.title: Mute notifications and touch grass
choices.body: The grass doesn't have engagement metrics. That's the point.

choices.title: Use AI to craft replies at scale
choices.body: Become a reply bot with a human avatar. The final form.

title: The Exit Sign in the Burning Building
body: An ex-colleague offers you a freelance retainer: two days a week, good money, no internal politics. It feels like seeing an exit sign in a burning building.

choices.title: Take the retainer and moonlight quietly
choices.body: Two jobs. One soul. See how long you can hold both.

choices.title: Bring a friend and build a tiny agency
choices.body: If you're going to jump, bring someone who can land.

choices.title: Decline and stay for stability and benefits
choices.body: The devil you know has dental insurance.

title: The Dashboard Nobody Reads
body: You built a beautiful marketing dashboard. Real-time metrics. Custom filters. Took two weeks. Leadership looked at it once. They still ask for "a quick update" via Slack every Monday. The dashboard loads to zero viewers.

choices.title: Send a weekly digest email that summarizes the dashboard
choices.body: If they won't go to the data, bring the data to their inbox.

choices.title: Automate the Monday update with AI and reclaim two hours
choices.body: Let a robot write the update nobody reads.

choices.title: Kill the dashboard and just talk to people
choices.body: Replace a tool with a conversation. Revolutionary.

title: Time to Rebrand Your Failures
body: Three campaigns flopped this quarter. Your ability REBRAND is tingling. You could frame this as "rapid experimentation" or "market learning" or "deliberate iteration." The words exist. The spin is available. Your integrity is optional.

choices.title: Rebrand it as a test-and-learn framework with actual insights
choices.body: Find the signal in the noise. Make the failure useful.

choices.title: Be honest about what didn't work and propose fixes
choices.body: Radical transparency. The kind that makes people uncomfortable.

choices.title: Bury it in a quarterly report nobody will read
choices.body: The best place to hide a body is page 47 of a PDF.

title: Your Slack Status Says Active But You Are Not
body: It's 9pm. Your Slack status shows green. Three people have messaged you. Your laptop is open because you forgot to close it. You are technically on the couch watching TV. You are also technically working.

choices.title: Answer the messages and accept you have no boundaries
choices.body: The green dot owns you. Respond. Be responsive. Be available. Be broken.

choices.title: Set your status to away and close the laptop
choices.body: Draw the line. The messages will be there tomorrow. So will you.

choices.title: Set up auto-replies and schedule sends for the morning
choices.body: Appear present while being absent. The ultimate marketing skill.

title: Your Personal Brand Is Bigger Than the Company's
body: Your LinkedIn posts get more engagement than the company account. The CMO noticed. She's either impressed or threatened. The meeting is in ten minutes and the calendar invite has no description.

choices.title: Offer to align your personal brand with company messaging
choices.body: Make your clout their clout. Everybody wins. Probably.

choices.title: Keep them separate and protect your independence
choices.body: Your audience followed you, not the brand. Keep it that way.

choices.title: Use the leverage to negotiate a raise or title bump
choices.body: If your brand has value, get paid for it.

title: One Person With AI Outbids Your Agency
body: Freelancer. Laptop. AI stack. She pitched your biggest client. Better proposal. 48-hour turnaround. Your team needed four weeks. No office. No employees. Claude, a Notion template, and a coffee shop in Denver. She's eating your lunch.

choices.title: Hire her and absorb her workflow into your team
choices.body: If you can't beat the one-woman army, recruit her.

choices.title: Restructure your team to be leaner and AI-native
choices.body: If one person can do it, maybe twelve people can't.

choices.title: Double down on relationships and service that a solo operator can't match
choices.body: She has AI. You have account dinners and institutional knowledge.

title: The Reorg Was Designed by an AI
body: All-hands invite. No agenda. Next day: new org chart. Generated by an AI that analyzed communication patterns and "collaboration density scores." Your team split across three departments. The AI says you're a bottleneck. It doesn't know you cover two underperformers and mentor three juniors. It only sees the Slack data.

choices.title: Challenge the AI's methodology in writing to leadership
choices.body: Fight the machine with context it couldn't see.

choices.title: Adapt to the new structure and prove the AI wrong through results
choices.body: Don't argue. Just outperform the prediction.

choices.title: Use the reorg as cover to leave for a role that values humans
choices.body: If AI is designing the org, maybe you're in the wrong org.

title: The "AI Strategist" Replaced You on the Exec Team
body: The AI Marketing Strategist got your seat at the exec table. His contribution: a dashboard. Your contribution: ten years of knowing what works. Leadership chose the dashboard. You now report to a man who recommends tools you already use. He calls you his "execution layer."

choices.title: Document every win and demand a comp review
choices.body: Build the case. Show the receipts. Refuse to be an execution layer.

choices.title: Quietly become indispensable to the strategist
choices.body: If he needs you more than you need him, the power shifts.

choices.title: Start interviewing for CMO roles at smaller companies
choices.body: Be the decision-maker somewhere else. Stop being someone's tool.

title: Craft Is Dead, Long Live Throughput
body: VP said it in team meeting: "If it takes more than 30 minutes, the process is broken." Blog posts. The AI pipeline publishes 40 a day. Each adequate. None good. Adequacy at scale beats excellence at low volume. Your four-hour masterpiece: 200 views. The AI sludge: 200,000.

choices.title: Accept the new math and become a throughput optimizer
choices.body: Quality lost. Volume won. Mourn and move on.

choices.title: Write the good stuff on your own time, for your own audience
choices.body: The company won't value this. Maybe strangers on the internet will.

choices.title: Make the case that quality content is now a luxury positioning
choices.body: Craft is dead for commodities. Craft is alive for premium. Pick a lane.

title: The Exit Interview Was Conducted by an AI
body: A colleague who resigned got her exit interview from an AI. It asked probing questions. It listened empathetically. It generated a "sentiment analysis report" for HR. She said it was the best conversation she'd had at the company in two years. The AI cared more than any manager did. Or at least performed caring better. The distinction is getting blurry.

choices.title: Push for human exit interviews as a matter of dignity
choices.body: People deserve to leave through a human door.

choices.title: Review the AI's aggregate data for patterns you missed
choices.body: The robot is listening to everyone leave. Maybe there's a signal.

choices.title: Share the anonymous feedback with your team before HR buries it
choices.body: Someone should say it. The AI said it. Now you say it louder.

title: Consultants Are Just AI With Business Cards
body: Your friend who got laid off is now an AI marketing consultant charging $300/hr. Her process: client sends a brief, she feeds it to Claude, she edits the output for 20 minutes, she invoices $1,500. She calls it "strategic curation." She made $180K last year. You made $82K doing the work she's automating. She wants you to join her. She says the word "leverage" a lot.

choices.title: Join her and become an AI arbitrage consultant
choices.body: Sell the edit layer. The client pays for judgment. The AI does the work.

choices.title: Start your own consulting practice with a different angle
choices.body: Same game, your rules. Build something that's actually yours.

choices.title: Stay employed and let the market sort out the grifters
choices.body: Consulting is a bubble. Bubbles pop. Salaries persist. Probably.

title: Every Piece of Content Already Exists
body: Blog post. Email marketing best practices. AI search returns 847,000 existing articles. 12,000 published this month. Nothing left to say. Every angle taken. Every hot take lukewarm. Content marketing hit heat death. Your job was creation. Now it's curation. Or deletion.

choices.title: Pivot to content subtraction — curate, reduce, distill
choices.body: The new skill isn't creating content. It's removing it.

choices.title: Go hyper-specific and own a niche nobody else is touching
choices.body: Can't compete in broad. Find the narrow. Go deep.

choices.title: Abandon content marketing entirely and try something physical
choices.body: If digital is infinite slop, go analog. Direct mail. Events. Walls.

title: Door-to-Door Marketing Is a Luxury Now
body: DTC brand hired door-to-door salespeople. Humans. Legs. Doors. Eye contact. They call it "artisan outreach." 50x digital cost per acquisition. 340% higher conversion. Retention off the charts. Physical human presence is a luxury channel now. Your title says "digital." Digital is the discount bin.

choices.title: Pitch a human touchpoint strategy to leadership
choices.body: Bodies in rooms. Handshakes. The premium play.

choices.title: Build a hybrid: AI for targeting, humans for closing
choices.body: Let the machine find the door. Let the human knock on it.

choices.title: Double down on digital and optimize for cost efficiency
choices.body: Not everyone can afford artisan outreach. Efficiency is your moat.

title: Your Top Creator Isn't a Person
body: Top influencer partner. 40% of referral traffic. Just exposed as entirely AI-generated. Face, voice, lifestyle — synthetic. Audience didn't know. Engagement was real. Person was not. Affiliate agreement with an LLC registered to a 19-year-old in his parents' basement.

choices.title: Keep the partnership — the ROI is real even if the person isn't
choices.body: The metrics don't care about metaphysics. Ship the numbers.

choices.title: End it and pivot to verified-human creators only
choices.body: If trust is the product, synthetic creators are a liability.

choices.title: Launch your own AI creator and cut out the middleman
choices.body: If a teenager can run a fake influencer, so can a Fortune 500.

title: The Board Only Wants AI Metrics Now
body: Board doesn't want impressions, CTR, or pipeline. They want "AI efficiency ratios." Output per prompt. Cost per AI-generated asset. Human-to-AI content ratio. Your measurement framework is obsolete. They're not asking if marketing worked. They're asking if the humans justified their existence versus the machines. You are one of the humans.

choices.title: Observe for a week before having opinions
