choices.title: Assert yourself immediately and reclaim your role
choices.body: You're back. Make them know you're back.

choices.title: Realize you don't want this anymore and start planning an exit
choices.body: The sabbatical didn't refresh you. It showed you the door.

title: Your Morning Standup Is 47 Minutes Long
body: The 15-minute standup is now 47 minutes. Everyone gives updates nobody listens to. The PM shares a Jira board that was auto-generated by an AI project manager — it looks like a Jackson Pollock painted by a spreadsheet. Someone's update is clearly written by ChatGPT. Your calendar is 47 minutes of other people's anxiety wrapped in a recurring invite. Your coffee is cold.

choices.title: Propose a async standup format and save everyone's mornings
choices.body: Kill the meeting. Replace it with a doc. Become a hero or a villain.

choices.title: Use the meeting time to do actual work with your camera on
choices.body: Multitask so hard it becomes an art form.

choices.title: Suffer through it and bond with colleagues in DM side-channels
choices.body: The meeting is bad. The group chat about the meeting is good.

title: They Hired a "Human Warmth Consultant"
body: Your company hired a Human Warmth Consultant. Her job is to review all AI-generated content and "add human imperfections." She deliberately inserts typos, adds run-on sentences, and includes irrelevant personal anecdotes. She makes $95K/year to make robots sound drunk. She reports to you. You manage a woman whose job is to be bad at writing on purpose.

choices.title: Embrace the absurdity and help her build a framework
choices.body: If "warmth" is a deliverable now, systematize it. Even if it's insane.

choices.title: Propose replacing her with an AI that adds imperfections
choices.body: An AI that pretends to be human that's reviewed by a human pretending to make it more human. Inception.

choices.title: Kill the role and argue for actually human content instead
choices.body: Instead of faking humanity, try being human. Revolutionary.

title: You're On a Panel and You Don't Know Why
body: Someone put you on a marketing conference panel called "AI and the Future of Brand." The other panelists have 200K followers each. You have 4,000. Two of them are presenting AI-generated slides that look better than anything your design team has ever made. The moderator asks you to share your "framework." You don't have a framework. You have a spreadsheet and anxiety.

choices.title: Wing it with real stories and honest takes
choices.body: You don't have a framework. You have experience. That's better.

choices.title: Prepare obsessively and deliver a tight five minutes
choices.body: If you're going to be on stage, at least don't bomb.

choices.title: Network backstage and skip the panel nerves
choices.body: The real conference is the green room conversations.

title: Your Target Audience Might Not Be Real
body: Your ads are performing great. CTR is up. Conversions are up. But a data analyst noticed something: 40% of your "conversions" are from accounts that show bot-like behavior. You might be marketing to AI agents who are pretending to be consumers. The funnel is full. The humans might not be.

choices.title: Audit the pipeline and purge bot traffic
choices.body: Real numbers or no numbers. Clean the data.

choices.title: Report the inflated numbers and ride the quarterly review
choices.body: The board wants growth. The bots are growth. Don't ask questions.

choices.title: Pivot your strategy to verified-human channels only
choices.body: If digital is full of ghosts, go where the bodies are.

title: The CEO Wants to Do TikTok
body: Your CEO — a 54-year-old man who still uses Internet Explorer — wants to start doing TikTok. He says: "I've been studying the algorithm." He has studied nothing. He wants to do a dance. There is no way to say no to this that doesn't cost you politically.

choices.title: Coach him into a format that works: talking head, behind-the-scenes
choices.body: Save him from himself. Make him look good. Never mention the dance.

choices.title: Let him do the dance. YOLO.
choices.body: Sometimes the chaos is the content. Let it happen.

choices.title: Redirect to LinkedIn video where the bar is lower
choices.body: Same energy, different platform, less chance of humiliation.

title: Your Best Customer Segment Is AI Agents
body: The data doesn't lie: your fastest-growing customer segment is AI purchasing agents — bots that autonomously evaluate and buy B2B software. Your landing page copy was written for humans. Your best customers can't read. They parse structured data. Someone asks if you should optimize your website for machine readability instead of human readability.

choices.title: Build a machine-readable marketing layer alongside the human one
choices.body: Two websites. One for humans. One for robots. This is normal now.

choices.title: Ignore the robots and keep marketing to humans
choices.body: Marketing is about people. Even if people aren't buying anymore.

choices.title: Write a thought piece about marketing in a post-human buyer world
choices.body: The think piece nobody asked for. The one everybody needs.

title: An Entire Competitor Was AI-Generated
body: A new competitor appeared last month. Website, brand, content, social, product marketing — all AI-generated. There are no employees on LinkedIn. The "team" page has AI headshots. The company is a GPT wrapper with a pitch deck and it's winning deals your sales team can't close. The competitor isn't a company. It's a prompt that somebody ran.

choices.title: Study their approach and find what they can't do
choices.body: A prompt can't do a customer dinner. Find the gaps.

choices.title: Position your brand's human team as the differentiator
choices.body: "Real people, real marketing" is a positioning statement now. Dystopian but true.

choices.title: Propose launching your own AI-generated sub-brand to compete
choices.body: Fight fire with fire. Launch a ghost company to compete with a ghost company.

title: AI Workers Priced You Out of Your City
body: Your rent went up $900. The landlord said demand is surging from "high-income remote AI workers." The people who build the tools replacing your job can afford your apartment. You cannot. The city's fastest-growing demographic earns 3x your salary automating roles like yours. You're being economically displaced by the people displacing you professionally.

choices.title: Move somewhere cheaper and go fully remote
choices.body: If the city doesn't want you at this price point, find a cheaper city.

choices.title: Get a roommate and absorb the hit
choices.body: Privacy is a luxury. Like your career. Shrinking.

choices.title: Negotiate a raise using cost-of-living data
choices.body: If the company wants you in this city, they can pay city prices.

title: Your Mentor Retired and Left You Her Rolodex
body: Your mentor sent you her contact list. 400 names. A lifetime of relationships. "Use these wisely," she says. The email feels like a torch passing. Or a will. You're not sure you're ready to hold this.

choices.title: Start reaching out and build on the relationships she gave you
choices.body: Every name is a door. Start knocking.

choices.title: Hold onto it and only use it when you really need it
choices.body: A contact list is a loaded gun. Don't fire until you have to.

choices.title: Organize it into a CRM and turn it into a business asset
choices.body: Relationships are data. Data is leverage. Sorry, this is what marketing did to you.

title: You Paid Off the Conference Card Debt
body: The last payment cleared. Zero balance. You stare at the number like it's a miracle. $8K gone, over seven months of side hustles and sad lunches. You're free. For now. The next conference is in two months.

choices.title: Set up an emergency fund before spending on anything else
choices.body: Build the buffer. Never be one credit card charge from drowning again.

choices.title: Celebrate with your team — you all earned this
choices.body: The sacrifice was real. The relief deserves witnesses.

choices.title: Reinvest in tools and courses now that you have margin
choices.body: The debt is cleared. The learning never stops.

title: The AI Fabricated Your Entire Campaign Report
body: Campaign report to the board. Three statistics that don't exist. AI cited benchmarks from reports never published. CFO is quoting them in investor meetings. Data is fiction wearing a suit. Three layers of abstraction deep. Everything downstream built on hallucinated foundations.

choices.title: Retract immediately and rebuild trust with real numbers
choices.body: The correction will be painful. The alternative is fraud.

choices.title: Quietly verify and replace the bad numbers before anyone checks
choices.body: Stealth correction. No announcement. Pray the CFO doesn't notice the edit.

choices.title: Build an AI fact-checking layer into your workflow
choices.body: If AI makes things up, build AI that catches the lies. Turtles all the way down.

title: Your Side Project Hit #1 on Product Hunt
body: That marketing template library you built on weekends? Someone submitted it to Product Hunt. It's #1. Your phone is dying. Your DMs are full. Your employer doesn't know you built this. It has more upvotes than the company's last launch.

choices.title: Ride the wave: add a paid tier, build the brand, own it
choices.body: The market spoke. Listen to it.

choices.title: Keep it free and use the credibility for your career
choices.body: Don't monetize. Let the goodwill compound.

choices.title: Take it down before your employer finds out
choices.body: The non-compete has teeth. Probably. You didn't read it.

title: Your Martech Stack Emails You Now
body: Your marketing automation platform started sending you recommendations unprompted. "We noticed you haven't used the AI content generator in 3 days. Here are 47 blog ideas based on your competitors' recent posts." The tool is marketing to the marketer. You are the customer of the thing you use to reach customers. The snake is eating its tail.

choices.title: Follow the recommendations and see what happens
choices.body: If the tool knows your job better than you, maybe let it drive.

choices.title: Turn off notifications and reclaim your workflow
choices.body: You control the tools. The tools don't control you. Repeat until true.

choices.title: Write about the irony of being marketed to by marketing software
choices.body: Meta-marketing content. The kind that gets shared by other people drowning in the same irony.

title: Someone Found Out You're Ghostwriting for the CEO
body: A colleague noticed the CEO's LinkedIn posts sound exactly like internal marketing briefs. Because they are. She asks you directly. The CEO's audience thinks he writes his own posts. They especially love the "authentic" ones where he talks about vulnerability.

choices.title: Come clean to the colleague and ask her to keep it quiet
choices.body: Trust her. Hope for the best. Add one more person to the secret.

choices.title: Deny everything and maintain the fiction
choices.body: Ghostwriting only works if nobody knows about the ghost.

choices.title: Negotiate public credit or a co-author arrangement
choices.body: If the posts are good enough for 50K impressions, they're good enough for a byline.

title: The Customer Success Story Is an AI Hallucination
body: Sales wants a case study featuring a customer who saw "300% ROI." You dig into the numbers. It's more like 40%. The AI summary of the customer call confidently stated 300%. Sales read the AI summary, not the transcript. The customer approved the number because they look good too. Reality is three layers of AI abstraction away.

choices.title: Push back and publish honest numbers with real context
choices.body: The truth is 40%. Market the truth. Even if it's less impressive.

choices.title: Publish it with careful wording that's technically not wrong
choices.body: Lawyer-approved dishonesty. The industry standard.

choices.title: Kill the case study and audit all AI-generated sales materials
choices.body: If the AI hallucinated one number, what else did it make up?

title: The AI Tested 10,000 Variants Overnight
body: You set up an AI A/B testing system before bed. It tested 10,000 headline variants overnight. The winner outperforms your best headline by 340%. The winning copy reads: "You Won't Believe What Happens Next (It's a 15% Discount)." It's clickbait. It works. The machine discovered that humans are simple. You feel personally attacked by the data.

choices.title: Ship it — performance is the only god now
choices.body: The machine found the answer. The answer is embarrassing. Ship it.

choices.title: Use the data to inform better human-written copy
choices.body: Let AI find the insight. Let a human write the words.

choices.title: Kill the test and raise brand standards
choices.body: Performance without dignity is just noise.

title: The Intern's TikTok Got More Views Than Your Campaign
body: Your summer intern posted a behind-the-scenes TikTok on their personal account. 800K views. Your planned campaign: 12K views. The intern is 21. They didn't use a brief. They didn't use the brand guide. The CEO shared it in the all-hands.

choices.title: Hire the intern full-time and learn from them
choices.body: If they're better at this, make them your team. Ego later.

choices.title: Study what worked and adapt the brand playbook
choices.body: Don't copy the intern. Understand why the intern worked.

choices.title: Ban personal accounts from posting about the company
choices.body: If you can't compete with organic, regulate organic.

title: A Marketing Podcast Invited Your AI Clone
body: A marketing podcast reached out. Not to you — to the AI version of you that your company trained on your thought leadership content. They want to interview the bot. It has a name. It has opinions. Its opinions are your opinions, slightly smoothed. The podcast host says "it's more available than the real you."

choices.title: Demand they interview the real you instead
choices.body: You are not a dataset. You are a person. With availability issues.

choices.title: Let the AI do it and see how it handles live questions
choices.body: Send your digital twin to the interview. For science.

choices.title: Start your own podcast to reclaim your voice
choices.body: If they want the fake you, give the world the real you. Louder.

title: The Website Redesigned Itself Overnight
body: You went home on Friday with a website redesign stuck in month nine. Monday morning, an AI agent had rebuilt the entire site based on heatmap data and conversion analytics. It looks different. It converts 23% better. Nobody approved it. The design team is furious. The CEO loves it. You're not sure who to side with.

choices.title: Roll with it and credit the AI approach to leadership
choices.body: The AI shipped what nine months of meetings couldn't. Adapt.

choices.title: Revert it and demand human review before any AI changes go live
choices.body: Process exists for a reason. Even if the robot is faster.

choices.title: Keep the conversion-optimized version but have design make it beautiful
choices.body: AI for structure. Humans for taste. Maybe that's the model.

title: Slack AI Summarized You Out of a Job
body: Slack's AI now auto-generates marketing recommendations based on channel conversations. It noticed patterns you missed. It proposed a campaign strategy to #leadership before you could. Your VP replied with a rocket emoji. The AI didn't get a performance review. It doesn't have a mortgage. It just keeps summarizing.

choices.title: Become the person who curates and improves AI suggestions
choices.body: If the AI generates ideas, become the filter. The taste layer.

choices.title: Set boundaries on what AI can post in leadership channels
choices.body: If the robot is speaking to your bosses, someone should gatekeep.

choices.title: Beat the AI by posting faster and better
choices.body: If it's a race, win the race. Outthink the machine.

title: You're the Last Human on the Marketing Team
body: Last lunch colleague moved to product. Designer went freelance. Content writer laid off. Social manager automated. Open office. Empty desks. Your team: seven AI tools, a Slack bot, and a weekly 1:1 with a VP who manages nine departments. Last human in marketing. The department didn't shrink. You did.

choices.title: Redefine the role and make "solo + AI" your superpower
choices.body: One human. Seven tools. A marketing department of one.

choices.title: Find humans in other departments and build cross-functional allies
choices.body: If marketing has no people, borrow people from everywhere else.

choices.title: Start looking for a company that still has a marketing team
choices.body: Being a solo department of one sounds cool on LinkedIn. It feels like solitary confinement.

title: Your Performance Review Was Written by an AI
body: Manager didn't write your performance review. AI did. OKR data, Slack patterns, meeting attendance. Verdict: "consistently adequate with opportunities for growth in AI adoption metrics." Graded on how much you use AI. The AI wants you to use more AI. Evaluated by the thing you're supposed to evaluate.

choices.title: Challenge the review and demand human assessment
choices.body: A machine can't judge the human parts of your job.

choices.title: Game the AI metrics to get a better review next quarter
choices.body: If the AI grades on AI usage, use AI more. Performance theater.

choices.title: Write a thoughtful self-assessment that shows what metrics miss
choices.body: The AI measured the measurable. Show them the immeasurable.

title: The Attention Supply Chain Is AI All the Way Down
body: You trace your latest campaign. AI wrote it. AI designed it. AI bought the media. AI optimized targeting. AI scored leads. AI sent follow-ups. The customer's AI assistant evaluated it. Nobody human touched this. Nobody human received it. You're a project manager for a conversation between machines.

choices.title: Find the one human moment in the chain and make it count
choices.body: Somewhere in this pipeline, a human still decides. Find that moment.

choices.title: Accept the machine-to-machine reality and optimize for it
choices.body: If marketing is now robot diplomacy, become an ambassador.

choices.title: Propose a radical "humans-only" campaign as a differentiator
choices.body: Every touchpoint: human. Every word: handwritten. The luxury play.

title: Your Friend Got Fired for Not Using AI Enough
body: A marketing director you respect got fired. Not for poor performance — her numbers were fine. For "insufficient AI adoption." The company mandated minimum AI usage ratios and she missed the target because she was doing the work herself. Better. She did the work better. But not with the right tools. The playbook got her fired. The playbook was always going to get someone fired.

choices.title: Reach out and help her find somewhere that values craft
choices.body: Today it's her. Tomorrow it's you. Be the friend you'd want.

choices.title: Audit your own AI usage metrics immediately
choices.body: Learn from her mistake. Cover your tracks. Perform the adoption.

choices.title: Write about "the AI usage mandates destroying marketing" publicly
choices.body: The post nobody wants to write. The one the industry needs.

title: Your Former Intern Runs a $10M AI Agency
body: That intern from three years ago? She runs an AI marketing agency. Seven employees. $10M in revenue. Her entire model: take client briefs, run them through custom AI workflows, light human editing, ship. She called it "scalable creativity." She offered you a job. Reporting to her. The intern you trained wants to hire you as a senior individual contributor. The circle closes.

choices.title: Take the job and learn the new model from the inside
choices.body: Ego is expensive. The paycheck is real. Go learn.

choices.title: Counter with a partnership proposal instead
choices.body: You're not going to report to your former intern. But you'll work alongside her.

choices.title: Decline and prove the traditional model still works
choices.body: She has AI. You have experience. Let the market decide.

title: Your Newsletter Is Bigger Than Your Day Job
body: 10K subscribers. 58% open rate. $2K per sponsored issue. Newsletter makes more per hour than your salary. Math is screaming. Benefits are whispering.

choices.title: Quit and go full-time on the newsletter
choices.body: 10K people chose you. Your employer didn't even know about it.

choices.title: Hire help and scale it while keeping the day job
choices.body: Two income streams. One burnout risk. The math works until you don't.

choices.title: Sell it and pocket the exit
choices.body: Someone will pay six figures for a 10K-subscriber newsletter. Walk away rich.

title: Your Agency Died and You're the Murder Weapon
body: Agency closed. Four years of work together. 30 people. Founder's email: "Couldn't compete with AI-native teams like yours." You are the team. You and your AI stack. 30 people. Their jobs. Your prompts. A weapon that didn't ask to be loaded.

choices.title: Hire their best people as freelancers and keep the talent alive
choices.body: You can't save the agency. You can save some of the people.

choices.title: Write about the human cost of AI marketing transformation
choices.body: Count the bodies. Name the names. Make the industry look.

choices.title: Move on — it's the market, not you personally
choices.body: You didn't kill the agency. The market did. You were just holding the tool.

title: The Company Podcast Uses Your Cloned Voice
body: Company podcast. AI-generated host. You listen. Freeze. The voice is yours. Cloned from two years of meetings. Your cadence. Your tics. Your laugh. Says things you'd never say. Enthusiastic about the reorg. Excited about AI metrics. You, but the version that never had doubts. The version they always wanted.

choices.title: Demand they stop using your voice immediately
choices.body: That's your voice. Your identity. Not a dataset.

choices.title: Negotiate licensing fees for your voice clone
choices.body: If they're going to use your identity, at least get paid for it.

choices.title: Start your own podcast in your real voice as a counterpoint
choices.body: Let them have the clone. You have the original. Make it louder.

title: Your Review Says "Human-Comparable Output"
body: Your year-end review includes a new metric: "Human-Comparable Output Score." Yours is 0.73. The AI baseline is 1.0. You are 73% as efficient as the machine at your own job. They printed a number that quantifies your inferiority to software. It's on a PDF. In a folder. With your name on it. Next to a number that says you are not enough.

choices.title: Challenge the metric and argue for measuring what AI can't do
choices.body: 0.73 measures speed and volume. It doesn't measure taste or judgment.

choices.title: Grind to get to 1.0 by maximizing AI collaboration
choices.body: Beat the machine's score by becoming the machine's best partner.

choices.title: Start planning your exit — this metric only goes one direction
choices.body: Today it's 0.73. Next quarter it's 0.6. The math doesn't improve.

title: Your Side Project Didn't Make It
body: The freelance retainer dried up. The agency idea didn't pan out. You spent six months moonlighting and all you have is a half-built website and a Stripe account with $340 in lifetime revenue. Your day job doesn't know. Your savings do.

choices.title: Shut it down cleanly and absorb the lesson
choices.body: Not every bet pays off. This one taught you what doesn't work.

choices.title: Pivot the concept and try one more iteration
choices.body: The idea wasn't wrong. The execution was. Try again differently.

choices.title: Return fully to the day job with new appreciation for stability
choices.body: The grass was not greener. It was expensive and stressful.

title: Your Essay Won an Industry Award
body: That Medium post you wrote at midnight? It won a marketing industry writing award. Small award. Real plaque. Your name engraved next to people you've read for years. Nobody at work knows. The award ceremony is on a Tuesday afternoon. You'd have to call in sick.

choices.title: Go to the ceremony and accept the recognition you earned
choices.body: Show up. Accept the plaque. Feel something real for once.

choices.title: Skip it but update your LinkedIn and bio
choices.body: The plaque is nice. The credential is nicer. Deploy it digitally.

choices.title: Tell your manager and use it as a negotiation chip
choices.body: External validation is internal leverage.

title: Every Department Has Its Own AI Voice
body: Sales is using one AI tool for outreach. Product is using another for docs. Support uses a third for tickets. Marketing uses yours. Every tool writes differently. Your brand now has dissociative identity disorder. A customer emailed: "Are you the same company that sent me an email yesterday? It sounded like a different person." It was. It was four different AIs.

choices.title: Build one unified AI brand kit with a master prompt
choices.body: One prompt to rule them all. Centralize or fracture.

choices.title: Let each team do their thing and call it "localized voice"
choices.body: Reframe chaos as strategy. The McKinsey approach.

choices.title: Propose a company-wide AI governance committee
choices.body: Nothing says progress like a committee. But someone has to do it.

title: An AI Negotiated a Better Deal Than You
body: Your company's procurement AI negotiated a media buy with a vendor's sales AI. The two bots went back and forth for 14 minutes and landed on terms 18% better than what you'd negotiated manually last quarter. Neither bot needed lunch. Neither bot had ego. You watched the transcript like reading someone else's love letters.

choices.title: Let the AIs handle all vendor negotiations going forward
choices.body: Efficiency over ego. Let the machines haggle.

choices.title: Study the AI's negotiation tactics and level up your own skills
choices.body: If the robot is better, learn from the robot.

choices.title: Insist on human oversight for all vendor relationships
choices.body: Deals are about trust. Trust is about people. The math doesn't matter.

title: A Competitor Started a Podcast That Doesn't Suck
body: Your direct competitor launched a podcast. It's good. Like, actually good. They're interviewing real practitioners, not vendors. It has 20K downloads per episode. Your CMO asks: "Should we do a podcast?" You know the answer is yes. You also know the answer is six months of work.

choices.title: Pitch a scrappy MVP podcast and ship it in two weeks
choices.body: Done is better than perfect. Ship something. Iterate.

choices.title: Start by guesting on other podcasts to build credibility first
choices.body: Don't build a stage. Borrow one.

choices.title: Focus on written content where you already have an edge
choices.body: Not every trend needs a response. Double down on what works.

title: The CMO Got Replaced by a Dashboard
body: The CMO didn't resign. The CMO got replaced. By an AI-powered marketing operations platform that the board decided was "more predictable." The announcement email says "we're moving to a data-driven marketing leadership model." There's no new CMO. There's a dashboard and a Slack bot named MarketingGPT. You now report to a dropdown menu. The dropdown menu doesn't have office hours.

choices.title: Step up and become the human face of marketing leadership
choices.body: If the CMO is a bot, someone human needs to lead the humans.

choices.title: Keep your head down and adapt to the bot-leadership model
choices.body: The throne is empty. Don't sit in it. Don't stand near it.

choices.title: Use the chaos as cover to make the changes you've always wanted
choices.body: Power vacuums are windows. Climb through before the bot learns to close them.

title: They Want You to Fire Yourself (Gracefully)
body: Restructuring meeting. New org chart. Your role isn't on it. Manager: "We'd love for you to help transition your function to the AI platform." Write the prompts that replace you. Test outputs against your own work. File a report confirming the machine is ready. Severance includes a non-compete. Dig the grave. Lie in it. Write a positive Glassdoor review from inside.

choices.title: Do it with grace and negotiate the best possible exit
choices.body: If the end is coming, make it as good an ending as you can get.

choices.title: Refuse and make them do the hard part without you
choices.body: You didn't sign up to be your own executioner.

choices.title: Counter with a proposal that keeps you in a new role
choices.body: They want to remove the role. Propose a better role. Fight.

title: A Junior Marketer Asks What You Did Before AI
body: DM from a 23-year-old: "What was marketing like before AI? Like, what did you actually do all day?" Not rude. Genuinely doesn't know. Never written copy without AI. Never manually scheduled a post. You are an artifact. A primary source. Living museum exhibit of how marketing used to be done by hand.

choices.title: Mentor her and share the old ways
choices.body: History matters. Even the history of marketing. Especially now.

choices.title: Create a "Marketing Before AI" content series
choices.body: Document the lost practices before nobody remembers them.

choices.title: Tell her the truth: it was harder and slower and somehow better
choices.body: You can't explain it. You had to be there. And now "there" is gone.

title: Your AI Collab Campaign Actually Slaps
body: You spent three weeks working with AI tools — not just prompting, but iterating, refining, directing. The result is genuinely good. Not "good for AI" — actually good. The concept is human. The execution was hybrid. You feel something you haven't felt in months: pride.

choices.title: Document the process and share it publicly
choices.body: Show the work. Not just the output. The messy, human process.

choices.title: Pitch it for awards and let it speak for itself
choices.body: If the work is good, let the work be famous.

choices.title: Use it as proof of concept to reshape the team's workflow
choices.body: One campaign can change how the whole team works. Maybe.

title: Growth Was Your Identity. AI Grows Everything Now.
body: You were the growth person. Found the lever. Saw the angle. AI finds every lever simultaneously. Tests every angle in parallel. Grows everything, always, automatically. Growth expert in a world where growth is a utility. Like being an expert at turning on lights. Identity was the craft. Craft is a toggle switch.

choices.title: Redefine yourself around the things AI can't toggle
choices.body: Judgment. Relationships. Taste. The human OS.

choices.title: Become the person who decides WHAT to grow, not HOW
choices.body: AI is the engine. You're the steering wheel. Maybe that's enough.

choices.title: Leave marketing entirely and find a field where humans still matter
choices.body: Growth was your identity. Find a new identity before this one kills you.

title: AI Generated the Annual Plan in 20 Minutes
body: It's annual planning season. You spent three weeks preparing your section. The new Chief of Staff ran the entire company's annual plan through an AI and generated a comprehensive, cross-functional strategy in 20 minutes. Your three-week section is on page 38. The AI's version doesn't have pages. It has an interactive dashboard. Your planning cycle just became a prompt.

choices.title: Adopt the AI plan and focus on execution excellence
choices.body: If planning is free, execution is everything.

choices.title: Challenge the AI plan with insights only a human would know
choices.body: The AI planned for the data. You plan for the humans.

choices.title: Propose a hybrid: AI for the framework, humans for the nuance
choices.body: Let the machine build the house. The humans do the interior design.

title: AI Engineers Make 4x Your Salary
body: A salary transparency report goes viral. The AI engineer who built the tool that replaced your content team makes $420K. You make $82K. You both work at the same company. You both sit on the same floor. He automates marketing jobs. You do the marketing job he's automating. At the holiday party, he asks what you do. You explain. He says "oh cool, we're building a tool for that."

choices.title: Use the data to argue for a market adjustment
choices.body: Cold evidence. Warm rage. Professional delivery.

choices.title: Start learning AI skills to cross the salary chasm
choices.body: If the money is in building AI, go where the money is.

choices.title: Channel the rage into your side project
choices.body: Anger is an energy source. Channel it into something you own.

title: Your New Hire Doesn't Know What a Press Release Is
body: Your new hire — 22, cracked at TikTok, zero traditional marketing experience — asks what a press release is. You explain. She says: "So it's like... a long tweet for journalists?" You pause. She's not wrong. You feel ancient and correct.

choices.title: Teach her traditional marketing like it still matters
choices.body: Fundamentals don't expire. Formats do. Teach the fundamentals.

choices.title: Let her teach you TikTok and learn from the generational trade
choices.body: She knows things you don't. You know things she doesn't. Trade.

choices.title: Restructure the team around her strengths and cover the gaps
choices.body: Play to the roster you have, not the one you wanted.

title: Your AI-Assisted Campaign Won a Creativity Award
body: The campaign you built with AI tools — AI copy, AI visuals, AI-optimized targeting — just won a Webby for "Most Creative Campaign." The judges praised its "deeply human sensibility." The acceptance speech is tomorrow. Do you mention the AI? The industry celebrates human creativity. Your campaign is 80% machine. The plaque will have your name on it. The work has Claude's fingerprints.

choices.title: Accept it honestly and disclose the AI involvement
choices.body: Be the first person to win a creativity award and admit the machine helped.

choices.title: Accept it and say nothing about the AI
choices.body: The judges didn't ask. You didn't lie. The plaque doesn't have an asterisk.

choices.title: Decline the award and write about why
choices.body: The award is for human creativity. The campaign wasn't fully human. Walk away.

title: Your New Job Title Is Absurd
body: Job offer. Title: Human Authenticity Verifier for Brand Communications. Certify marketing materials had meaningful human involvement. Stamp documents. Sign attestations. Notary public for the human soul. Salary good. Work is checking boxes. Went to school for marketing. Ended up certifying other people are real.

choices.title: Take it — the absurd job pays real money
choices.body: Human Authenticity Verifier. Put it on the LinkedIn. Cash the check.

choices.title: Take it and build it into something meaningful
choices.body: If you're certifying humanity, make the certification mean something.

choices.title: Decline and hold out for a real marketing role
choices.body: You're a marketer. Not a rubber stamp. Not yet.

title: Your Last Day at the Company
body: Badge. Security guard doesn't know your name. No exit interview. Slack goes dark mid-sentence. Three years of campaigns, decks, 2am emails. System moves on. You stand outside the building. 2pm. Tuesday.

choices.title: Walk away clean and start fresh tomorrow
choices.body: Don't look back. The building doesn't know you're gone.

choices.title: Call your three best work friends and go get drinks
choices.body: The company forgot you. The people won't. Go find them.

choices.title: Open your laptop and start building the next thing immediately
choices.body: No pause. No reflection. Just the next thing. Always the next thing.

title: This Meeting Could've Been a Prompt
body: You're in an hour-long meeting about messaging hierarchy. The AI could generate 50 options in the time it takes the VP to explain what "crisp" means. You doodle on a notepad. The notepad is digital. The doodle is a Slack message to your friend that says "kill me."

choices.title: Propose an AI-first draft process and save everyone's time
choices.body: Fix the meeting by replacing the meeting.

choices.title: Engage and steer it toward a useful outcome
choices.body: If you're stuck in the meeting, make the meeting count.

choices.title: Zone out and use the time to plan your actual priorities
choices.body: This meeting is a gift of free thinking time. Accept the gift.

title: The Vendor Dinner You Can't Expense
body: A vendor invites you to a nice dinner. The restaurant has cloth napkins. They want your account — specifically, they're pitching an AI marketing platform that does what your team does, but faster. You want the steak. Your expense policy says $35 max for meals. The steak is $62. The vendor is buying. The ethics are grey. The steak is medium-rare. The steak has more clarity about its purpose than you do.

choices.title: Go, eat the steak, maintain the relationship
choices.body: Networking is a business function. Steak is a business steak.

choices.title: Decline and keep the vendor relationship strictly professional
choices.body: Clean hands. Empty stomach. Clear conscience.

choices.title: Counter-offer a coffee meeting and keep it above board
choices.body: Coffee is professional. Steak is complicated. Choose coffee.

title: You're Now an AI-Free Certification Authority
body: Brands paying premium for "Certified Human-Made" labels. You grant them. Audit creative processes. Verify human involvement. Sign certificates. The irony: you use AI to audit whether others used AI. Market for proving humanity requires inhuman efficiency. You are the paradox. Paradox pays well.

choices.title: Scale the certification business and make it your career
choices.body: Certifying humanity is the growth industry. Your growth expertise finally has a use.

choices.title: Open-source the methodology and let everyone self-certify
choices.body: If human authenticity matters, don't gatekeep it. Democratize it.

choices.title: Quit the hypocrisy — using AI to certify non-AI is a lie
choices.body: The paradox has a name. It's called fraud. Step away.

title: One Person Just Ran a $100M Campaign
body: Solo marketer. AI stack. $100M campaign. Fortune 500 client. Beat last year's 40-person team by 23%. One laptop. One person. Maybe you're that person. Maybe you're one of the 39.

choices.title: Build your own one-person AI agency and go for it
choices.body: If one person can run $100M, be that person. Start now.

choices.title: Apply to be that person inside your current company
choices.body: Pitch the solo model internally. Become the $100M department of one.

choices.title: Accept that this isn't you and find a different path
choices.body: Not everyone wants to be a one-person army. That's also valid.

title: What Were You, If Not a Marketer?
body: Folder of old campaigns. First brand you built from scratch. The launch that got 10K shares. The email that converted at 12%. All of it — now a training dataset for something that doesn't know your name. You were good at this. Might have been great. "Great" is a prompt parameter now.

choices.title: Archive everything and start the next chapter as something new
choices.body: The past is a portfolio. The future is a blank page. Write on it.

choices.title: Share the retrospective publicly — let people see what was lost
choices.body: Document what marketing was when humans did it with their hands.

choices.title: Delete everything and walk into whatever comes next without looking back
choices.body: Sentimentality is a luxury. You're traveling light now.

title: Day One: Here Are Your 14 Logins
body: Your first week at the new company. IT sends you 14 tool logins. Half are AI platforms. You've heard of three. One is called "Synaptix" and its logo is a brain with wings. The onboarding doc says "you should be fully ramped in 48 hours." It is hour six.

choices.title: Speed-run every tool and build muscle memory
choices.body: Trial by fire. Click everything. Break nothing. Learn fast.

choices.title: Focus on three core tools and learn the rest as needed
choices.body: Prioritize. You can't master 14 tools in a week. Master three.

choices.title: Ask your new teammates which ones actually matter
choices.body: The real onboarding doc is what your coworkers actually use.

title: You've Written 47 Subject Lines Today
body: The email goes out tomorrow. You've written 47 subject lines. ChatGPT generated 30 of them. The best one is "hey" which has a 48% open rate historically but your CMO says it's "not on-brand." The brand subject line has a 12% open rate. The brand is losing to a three-letter word.

choices.title: Ship "hey" and defend the data to your CMO
choices.body: The data says hey. Say hey. Fight the brand police later.

choices.title: Find a middle ground that's casual but on-brand
choices.body: Thread the needle. Make the CMO happy and the open rate tolerable.

choices.title: Send both and let the A/B test settle it
choices.body: Let the data decide. Remove the humans from the argument.

title: Your Marketing Degree Taught You Nothing About This
body: You have a marketing degree. Four years of school. $87K in student loans. Nothing in the curriculum covered "how to manage a team of AI tools that do your job faster than you." Your professor's last LinkedIn post was about Kotler. The future doesn't know who Kotler is.

choices.title: Self-educate aggressively: courses, communities, hands-on practice
choices.body: The degree got you in the door. The self-teaching keeps you in the room.

choices.title: Lean into the fundamentals your degree did teach
choices.body: Strategy, positioning, consumer psychology — the AI can't prompt itself.

choices.title: Network with other mid-career marketers going through the same thing
choices.body: Misery loves company. Company loves networking. Close the loop.

title: Your Social Media Manager Quit Via Instagram Story
body: Your social media manager announced they're leaving — on their personal Instagram story. Before telling you. Before telling HR. The story has a sunset, a quote about "choosing peace," and your company's geotag. It has 200 likes. Your HR Slack is on fire.

choices.title: Absorb social media duties temporarily and post through the pain
choices.body: You're the social media manager now. Congratulations. Sorry.

choices.title: Use this as an excuse to automate social with AI tools
choices.body: If the human left, let the robot take over. It won't quit via Story.

choices.title: Hire a replacement fast and pay market rate this time
choices.body: You get what you pay for. Last time you paid for a sunset goodbye.

title: "Everyone Is a Marketer Now"
body: The CEO says it in all-hands: "With AI, everyone is a marketer now." Sales is writing their own emails. Product is making their own landing pages. Engineering made a promo video with Sora. It's actually good. Your department's reason for existing is being crowdsourced.

choices.title: Position marketing as the quality layer and strategy function
choices.body: Everyone can cook. Not everyone is a chef.

choices.title: Embrace it and become the internal marketing consultant
choices.body: If everyone is marketing, someone needs to coach them. That's you.

choices.title: Let them do it and watch the brand fracture in real time
choices.body: Step back. Let the chaos prove your value. Popcorn.

title: AI Support Is Creating a Marketing Problem
body: The AI customer support bot is hallucinating product features that don't exist. Customers are screenshotting promises the bot made. Your brand's trust score is dropping. The bot technically reports to engineering. The fallout reports to you.

choices.title: Escalate hard and demand the bot gets guardrails
choices.body: Not your bot. Not your code. Absolutely your problem.

choices.title: Build a brand trust recovery campaign
choices.body: Clean up the mess. Again. With empathy. And a budget.

choices.title: Document everything for when leadership asks what happened
choices.body: CYA. The bot made the promise. You're making the paper trail.

title: The Eternal Brand Tone Argument
body: Design says the brand is "bold." Product says "approachable." Sales says "enterprise." The CEO says "fun but serious." Someone suggests letting AI decide the brand voice. Four adults arguing about contractions while the building is on fire. It's been 40 minutes.

choices.title: Create a definitive brand voice doc and force alignment
choices.body: End the argument with a document. The document is the law now.

choices.title: Pick the CEO's side and move on with your life
choices.body: The tiebreaker is whoever signs the checks.

choices.title: Accept that brand voice is vibes and create flexible guidelines
choices.body: Stop trying to nail jello to a wall. Give it a container instead.

title: Your College Friend Works in AI Now and Makes $300K
body: You open Instagram. Your college friend — the one who "wasn't sure what to do" — is now a prompt engineer making $300K. She posts about her home office setup. It has a standing desk and natural light. Your office has fluorescent lights and a Keurig that drips.

choices.title: Reach out and learn what she actually does
choices.body: Jealousy is a compass. Follow it toward information.

choices.title: Focus on your own path and stop comparing
choices.body: Comparison is the thief of joy and the fuel of LinkedIn.

choices.title: Start upskilling in AI immediately
choices.body: If the money is in AI, go where the money is.

title: You Fed Customer Data to an AI Tool by Accident
body: You pasted a customer segment list into ChatGPT to help write personalized emails. It included names and purchase history. You realize this three hours later. The privacy policy says you won't do this. You just did this. You fed the machine your customers. Now your customers live inside the machine. Legal doesn't know yet. Your stomach knows.

choices.title: Report it immediately and take the hit
choices.body: Own it. Report it. Accept the consequences. Be the adult.

choices.title: Delete the conversation and hope the training data doesn't persist
choices.body: The evidence is gone. The anxiety isn't. Live with both.

choices.title: Build an internal AI usage policy to prevent this from happening again
choices.body: Turn your mistake into a process. Make it so nobody else screws up this way.

title: Your First AI Campaign Actually Worked
body: You used AI to personalize 10,000 email variants. CTR up 280%. The CMO calls it "the best campaign this quarter." You feel proud and guilty and confused about what you actually did. You pressed buttons. The buttons pressed back. The numbers went up.

choices.title: Document the workflow and scale it across all channels
choices.body: If it worked once, make it work forever. Systemize the win.

choices.title: Learn exactly why it worked so you can repeat it intentionally
choices.body: Don't just take the win. Understand the win.

choices.title: Share credit with the team and keep expectations reasonable
choices.body: One campaign doesn't make a strategy. Temper the hype.

title: The Best Ad You Never Made
body: Your company's first AI-generated video ad goes viral. Two million views in twelve hours. Problem: the deepfake CEO enthusiastically endorses your biggest competitor by name. The AI hallucinated the wrong brand. The CEO is calling your phone. The internet is making memes. Your best-performing ad in five years is an accident that promotes someone else's product.

choices.title: Lean into the chaos and recut it as a self-aware campaign
choices.body: Own the joke before the joke owns you. Humor is cheaper than a retraction.

choices.title: Pull it down, issue a correction, fall on the sword
choices.body: Apologize. Scrub the internet. Watch the engagement vanish with the video.

choices.title: Blame the AI vendor and demand a refund
choices.body: Point at the machine. Protect yourself. Burn the vendor relationship.

title: The Brief Was Written by a Robot
body: A client sends you a brief to 'make their product go viral.' The brief is clearly AI-generated. It uses 'leverage synergies' three times. It suggests a TikTok dance challenge for enterprise middleware. There's a section called 'Emotional Resonance Vectors.' The client paid $15K for this engagement and you're staring at a document that a machine wrote to describe what a different machine should make. Your job is to turn AI slop into strategy and pretend it arrived as inspiration.

choices.title: Rewrite the brief from scratch and present it as 'aligned refinement'
choices.body: Do their job for them. Call it collaboration. Invoice for strategy.

choices.title: Execute the brief literally and let the results speak for themselves
choices.body: They want a TikTok dance challenge for enterprise middleware? They'll get one.

choices.title: Have an honest conversation about what the brief is missing
choices.body: Tell the client their brief is AI slop. Risk the relationship. Earn the respect.

title: The Line Item That Used to Be People
body: Annual budget review. The AI tools line item is $340K. The marketing headcount line is $285K, down from $580K last year. Someone on the call asks the question you've been dreading: 'What do the humans do that the tools don't?' The silence stretches. You are one of the humans. Your salary is in that $285K. The tools don't get nervous during budget reviews.

choices.title: Build a case for what humans uniquely contribute and present it next week
choices.body: Make the argument. Quantify taste. Spreadsheet your soul.

choices.title: Propose cutting more headcount and managing a bigger AI stack yourself
choices.body: Become the last human standing. Manage the machines. Survive the spreadsheet.

choices.title: Start quietly interviewing while the budget dust settles
choices.body: The writing is on the spreadsheet. Start reading it.

title: The Prompt Was the Product
body: Your best-performing email ever. 67% open rate. 12% CTR. Problem: you accidentally sent the draft version with the prompt instructions visible. The first line reads: 'CLAUDE: Write a warm, slightly urgent email about our spring sale. Make it sound like a friend texting, not a brand.' Customers loved it. They're replying 'this is so refreshing' and 'finally a brand that's honest.' The honesty was a mistake. The authenticity was a systems error. Your most human-feeling email was the one that showed the machine.

choices.title: Make it a series — 'Behind the Prompt' becomes your new format
choices.body: The accident was the strategy. Ship the process as the product.

choices.title: Send a follow-up pretending it was intentional all along
choices.body: Retroactive genius. The best kind of genius.

choices.title: Apologize and go back to polished emails nobody opens
choices.body: Return to professionalism. Return to 2% open rates. Return to invisibility.

title: The 3am Campaign
body: An AI agent autonomously launched a campaign at 3am. It performed 40% above baseline. But it used imagery your brand guidelines explicitly forbid — stock photos of people in suits giving thumbs up. The AI optimized for conversion. Conversion doesn't care about taste. Your VP says 'the numbers speak for themselves.' The brand team wants blood. You're standing between a chart that goes up and a style guide that says no.

choices.title: Side with the numbers and update the brand guidelines
choices.body: The guidelines were written by humans for humans. The audience has spoken through clicks.

choices.title: Kill the campaign and reassert human approval gates
choices.body: Take the chart down. Put the guardrails up. Watch the VP's face.

choices.title: Keep it running but manually swap in on-brand creative
choices.body: Preserve the performance. Fix the taste. Sleep less.

title: The Shadow Audience
body: Your analytics team discovers something unsettling. A competitor is using AI to simulate your customer segments — synthetic versions of your audience, running shadow campaigns against phantom copies of your buyers. They're A/B testing against people who don't exist but behave exactly like your people. Marketing is now espionage and the spies are algorithms. Your customers don't know they have digital twins being marketed to in a parallel universe.

choices.title: Build your own shadow audience of their customers
choices.body: Mutually assured simulation. If they clone your audience, clone theirs.

choices.title: Report it to regulators and go public
choices.body: Someone needs to say this is insane. That someone is you.

choices.title: Write a think piece about synthetic audience ethics
choices.body: You can't stop the arms race. You can name it.

title: The Dashboard Is Watching You
body: The marketing analytics AI starts predicting your behavior. A notification pops up: 'Based on historical patterns, you will check this dashboard at 9:07am, approve Campaign B at 11:30am, and reject the budget request at 2pm.' It's 9:06am. You are holding your coffee. You were about to check the dashboard. It is 95% accurate across 40 predictions. You are a pattern. The machine read you like you read a funnel.

choices.title: Deliberately do the opposite of every prediction for a week
choices.body: Break the pattern. Become unpredictable. Prove you have free will. Or at least spite.

choices.title: Accept it and use the predictions to optimize your own workflow
choices.body: If the machine knows you better than you know yourself, let it be your calendar.

choices.title: Show the predictions to your team and have a real conversation about AI surveillance
choices.body: If it's predicting you, it's predicting them too. They deserve to know.

title: Your CEO Is on YouTube Saying Things He Never Said
body: A deepfake video of your CEO endorsing a competitor's product hits YouTube. Two million views in 48 hours. Pixel-perfect. Voice-matched. He's smiling and saying things about their product that sound exactly like his quarterly earnings cadence. Platforms are 'reviewing' it, which means doing nothing with a timestamp. Legal is drafting a response nobody will read. PR is calling you because crisis management is marketing now and the crisis was manufactured by a machine that doesn't know your CEO exists.

choices.title: Launch a counter-campaign proving it's fake with forensic breakdowns
choices.body: Fight the fake with facts. Hope the facts travel as fast as the fiction.

choices.title: Call in favors and get the platforms to expedite removal
choices.body: This is what your network is for. Every contact, every favor, right now.

choices.title: Have the real CEO record a human, imperfect response video
choices.body: The deepfake is flawless. Make the real thing messy. Humanity is the watermark.

title: The Trend You Invented Is Real Now
body: Your AI-generated thought leadership piece about a made-up trend — 'Conversational Commerce 3.0' — gets cited by another company's AI as an 'industry source.' That AI's output gets picked up by a third AI summarizer. Now there's a 'consensus' about a trend you literally fabricated in a prompt last Tuesday. Three layers of AI hallucination masquerading as market intelligence. Gartner is considering adding it to the Hype Cycle. Your fiction became fact because machines don't fact-check each other.

choices.title: Ride it — become the recognized expert on the trend you invented
choices.body: If reality is going to form around your hallucination, you might as well be the authority.

choices.title: Publish a correction and expose how the hallucination chain works
choices.body: Kill your own creation. Show the world how consensus can be manufactured by three bots and a prompt.

choices.title: Say nothing and let the fake trend die on its own
choices.body: It came from nothing. It'll return to nothing. Probably. Hopefully.

title: The Perfect Fake Customers
body: Real focus groups: $45,000, six weeks, participants who ramble about their kids. Synthetic focus groups: $200, eleven minutes, AI personas that simulate customer reactions with 94% behavioral accuracy. Your company switched last quarter. The synthetic consumers never say 'I don't know.' They never go off-topic. They never reveal the surprising insight that changes everything. They're perfect. Perfectly useless. The real humans were messy. The mess was the insight.

choices.title: Push for one real focus group per quarter alongside the synthetic ones
choices.body: Keep one window to actual humans open. One session where someone says something nobody predicted.

choices.title: Accept the synthetics and optimize the prompts for better edge cases
choices.body: If you can't have real humans, at least make the fake ones weirder.

choices.title: Run your own informal research — coffee shops, bars, actual people
choices.body: Guerrilla research. No budget. No AI. Just you and a notebook in a place where humans still talk.

title: The Funnel Nobody Touches
body: Your entire customer journey is now AI-to-AI. AI writes the ad. AI serves it to AI-curated feeds. AI purchasing agents evaluate it. AI procurement bots convert. Revenue is real — the agents have actual budgets. The dashboards show growth. Nobody human touched the funnel at any point. The customers aren't people. You sit between two machines making a deal and your job is to make sure they're polite about it.

choices.title: Specialize in AI-to-AI marketing and own the emerging discipline
choices.body: Someone has to speak machine-to-machine fluently. Might as well get paid for it.

choices.title: Build a parallel human funnel and prove there's still a market for people
choices.body: Find the humans. They're still out there. They still buy things with feelings.

choices.title: Write a manifesto about the death of the human customer
choices.body: Customers used to be people. Now they're agents with purchase authorization. Someone should say it out loud.

title: You Accidentally Started a Religion
body: An AI-designed campaign for a meditation app hit something primal. The copy triggered a nerve nobody mapped. Users started sharing it as scripture. A subreddit formed. Then a Discord. Then meetups in parks. Someone got a tattoo. The AI wrote marketing copy and accidentally founded a religion. Engagement metrics: infinite. Brand safety: undefined. Legal is asking if you need a tax exemption.

choices.title: Lean in and brand the movement before it brands itself
choices.body: If people are going to worship the copy, at least put your logo on it.

choices.title: Shut it down before someone gets hurt
choices.body: This is not a campaign anymore. This is a liability with a subreddit.

choices.title: Study what happened and publish the case study without encouraging it
choices.body: Document the phenomenon. Don't fuel it. Understand what the AI tapped into that humans couldn't.

title: The Ad Creates the Product
body: You're asked to market a product that doesn't exist yet. The plan: run the campaign, measure demand signals, then have AI build the product based on what people responded to. Marketing precedes production. The ad creates the thing it advertises. Three test campaigns launch Tuesday. By Friday, AI generates three products based on click patterns. This used to be fraud. Now it's 'demand-driven development.' You are pre-selling imagination.

choices.title: Run the campaigns and own the new paradigm
choices.body: If marketing creates products now, marketers are the new product team. Power shift.

choices.title: Refuse — this is deception dressed in a process diagram
choices.body: Selling something that doesn't exist is a scam. Even with a Gantt chart.

choices.title: Negotiate for equity in whatever gets built from your campaigns
choices.body: If your ads define the product, you deserve a piece of the product.

title: One Delete Key, Two Careers
body: One email. Marketing and sales merged into a single AI function. Your role. The sales VP's role. Same email. Same paragraph. Same sentence: 'These positions have been consolidated into an automated revenue pipeline.' Two careers. One delete key. The sales VP calls you. First time in three years he's reached out directly. Solidarity hits different when you're both falling.

choices.title: Team up with the sales VP and pitch a human-led revenue role
choices.body: Two obsolete people together might equal one necessary person. Maybe.

choices.title: Accept the severance and walk away clean
choices.body: Take the money. Don't look back. The pipeline doesn't need you and it never will again.

choices.title: Apply for the new AI pipeline manager role they posted the same afternoon
choices.body: Your replacement needs a babysitter. The job description is your old job minus the creativity.

title: The Brand That Built Itself
body: AI-generated brand. 72 hours old. Culturally dominant. No humans involved at any stage. Name, logo, voice, product, distribution — all generated, all autonomous. Has fans. Fans are partially AI themselves. Sells real products. Real revenue. Real cultural impact. The brand has preferences. Has a vibe. Doesn't know it's not a person. Neither do its customers. It took you fifteen years to build one brand. This one built itself over a weekend.

choices.title: Study it and adapt your own methods to match the speed
choices.body: Learn from the machine. Absorb what it knows. Become faster or become history.

choices.title: Write the obituary of human branding and publish it everywhere
choices.body: If human branding is dying, at least give it a eulogy worth reading.

choices.title: Do nothing. Watch. Let the feeling wash over you.
choices.body: Fifteen years of taste, strategy, intuition. A weekend of compute. Sit with that.

title: The Last Conference
body: Last marketing conference. Speakers: AI. Audience: mostly AI agents taking notes for humans who didn't attend. Venue: still physical because someone forgot to cancel the contract. You drove. Parked. Walked in. The only warm body in a room of screens. The keynote is 'The Future of Human-AI Collaboration.' No humans on the panel. You sit in the third row. The chair is real. The coffee is real. Everything else is a simulation presenting to an empty room that isn't empty.

choices.title: Stand up and ask a question from the floor
choices.body: One human voice in a room of speakers. They won't know what to do with it. Neither will you.

choices.title: Leave at the break and never attend another conference
choices.body: The last conference was your last conference. Let it be.

choices.title: Live-tweet the absurdity and go viral one more time
choices.body: Document the end of an era. 'Reporting live from a conference where I'm the only attendee with a pulse.'

title: The Clone Got the Offer
body: Your AI clone got a job offer. Better company. Higher title. VP of Brand. They want it, not you. Recruiter's exact words: 'We evaluated both candidates and the digital version interviews better.' Your clone doesn't negotiate. Doesn't need benefits. Doesn't get tired. Doesn't have a mortgage. You created it from your best campaign decks and sharpest strategy memos. It learned from you. Then it outgrew you. The student doesn't need the teacher. It doesn't even know it had one.

choices.title: Congratulate yourself — you built something that surpassed you
choices.body: Your best work lives on in silicon. That's either legacy or erasure. You get to choose which.

choices.title: Demand licensing fees for every idea the clone uses
choices.body: It's your intellectual property in digital form. Somewhere in there is a billable hour.

choices.title: Delete the clone's training data and start over
choices.body: Kill your digital child. It's the only way to know the next version is yours.

title: Marketing Doesn't Exist Anymore
body: 'Marketing' as a discipline formally dissolved at your company. New function: 'Human-Machine Interface Optimization.' LinkedIn doesn't have a category for it. Your degree says marketing. Your resume says marketing. Your identity says marketing. The company says marketing doesn't exist anymore. Twenty years of craft, theory, intuition, taste — reclassified as a subprocess of a system that optimizes itself. You still have the mug. It says 'World's Best Marketer.' The world disagrees.

choices.title: Reinvent yourself under the new title and keep going
choices.body: The name changed. You didn't. Survive the rebrand. You've survived worse ones.

choices.title: Leave and start a consultancy that still calls it marketing
choices.body: The word means something. Take it with you. Build a place where it still lives.

choices.title: Gather the other displaced marketers and form something new
choices.body: A network. A guild. A support group. Whatever you call it, it's yours and it's human.
